title: Mobile games to Steam transition
author: BrownaroStudios
selftext:
Has anyone started making mobile games and then decided they want to also make the games available on Steam or to focus on Steam instead?

We've been shipping on iOS and Android for a while now and I keep coming back to the idea of putting some of our games on Steam too. Godot handles desktop exports so the engine side isn't the concern. It's more the business side I'm trying to figure out.

A few things I'd love to hear about from anyone who's done it:

* How hard is the actual transition? Not the export itself but the stuff around it. Store pages, marketing, input changes, screen sizes, all that.  Are there APIs that can handle this as well?
* Is the monetization better? Mobile is free to play with ads and small IAPs. Steam seems to want a paid up front model which is a totally different thing.
* Has anyone found one works better than the other for the same game?
* What surprised you? Discoverability, audience expectations, refund rates, review culture, anything you didn't expect going in.
* Did you keep both platforms going or end up picking one?

Trying to figure out if this is worth the effort or if we'd be better off just doubling down on mobile.

comments.author: zayelion
comments.body: I recommend staying on mobile for 1 to 2 years. Steam will want a disclosure and you lose 30% of users.

replies.author: BrownaroStudios
replies.body: When you say a disclosure, what kind of disclosure are you referring to?  AI usage?

comments.author: NovaGamingX4
comments.body: Steam is rough bc its 100 dollars per game release

replies.author: zayelion
replies.body: I actually think this needs to be increased. The flood of games is making marketing them harder.
